title: Josie Baff wins women’s snowboard cross Olympic gold to make history for Australia
content:
LIVIGNO, Italy — Josie Baff didn’t care about the storybooks that were supposed to be written. She didn’t care that beloved Italian snowboard cross star Michela Moioli was supposed to win on her home course to pen a storia d’amore. She didn’t care that Eva Adamczyková’s comeback was the stuff of legends.

Though ranked No.2 in the world, the 23-year-old came from out of nowhere to win a gold medal that no one, including herself, seemed to see coming.

After finishing 17th in the morning’s seeding runs, the Australian survived a series of knockout runs, having a hand in the exits of stars like Charlotte Bankes, the world number one, and Julia Nirani-Pereira, and reached a loaded finals race with Moioli and Adamczyková.

Baff, a snowboarder since age 2, the daughter of a ski and snowboard instructor, rode a flawless ride to victory, snatching an early lead in the final race, and stretching it to an advantage no one could close. Adamczyková got close in the end, but came up short, leaving Baff to cross the line with both hands in the air and disbelief on her face.

The gold was the first by an Australian woman in snowboard cross. In Baff’s only other Olympic appearance, she finished 18th in the Sochi Games in her individual race and 13th in mixed cross with Adam Lambert.

Before Baff took to the podium in Livigno, Adamczyková leapt into her spot as silver medalist with her arms raised and customary fake mustache stenciled above her top lip. It had been a long, long road there.

A little over four years ago, in the qualifying season leading up the 2022 Beijing Olympic Games, the Czech star found herself in a close, tense race in a World Cup event in Montafon, Austria. Never one to back down, Adamczyková went for it, diving feet-first into the line for every millimeter of a photo finish. Skimming the snow on her back, she pressed down her board to slow and caught not only an edge, but a terrible twist of fate. In a single snap, Adamczyková broke both her ankles.

The moment not only shattered her hopes for the 2022 Games, but also felt like a possible downturn for a career that had exploded years earlier with Adamczyková’s gold medal in the 2014 Sochi Games.

Friday’s silver carried weight.

Moioli, meanwhile, celebrated another medal for Italy in these Games and drew massive cheers. The 2025 world champion and 2018 Olympic champion was electric throughout the day’s racing both on the course, advancing with relative ease, and off the course, waving her arms to pump up the home crowd.

Charlotte Bankes’ day couldn’t have been more different. The Briton’s decorated career is missing an Olympic medal and it was hoped her fourth appearance in the Games might be magic. But the day never came together. A rough run in the Round of 32 required a comeback to advance and a fourth-place quarterfinal appearance left her fighting emotions in the end.

Now Bankes’ medal hopes move to the mixed team race. She’ll pair with 24-year-old Huw Nightingale.

Faye Thelen was the top American finisher, reaching Friday’s semifinals, for one of her top showing in a snowboarding career that began with a first appearance in a FIS event at age 14. Thelen, 33, is not far removed from having her second child and was all smiles following her semifinal loss.

Baff can go for more hardware on Saturday for another run in the mixed team event.
